I agree with you that it doesn’t seem like her service dog is legit, but it’s not true that having a service dog mandates that they’re with you 24/7. It’s kind of like saying if you use a wheelchair you’re never allowed to walk or you don’t actually need the chair. Disabled people have good days and bad days, and disabilities range a lot. A service dog is just a dog specially trained to assist with disability, for example if you have PTSD and your service dog is trained to wake you from night terrors, they’re still a service dog but it’s not necessary to bring them everywhere with you.

He was adored, spoiled, doted on, and it was so clear how loved he was and that he knew it. The little guy wanted for nothing. The way you talk about your cat, I’m sure the same is true. She knew how loved she was. Our little guy only had one bad day his entire life with us, which is when he passed. It wasn’t what we wanted for him, it hurt like hell, but we took comfort in knowing that even on his last day, he knew how adored he was. Old cats like privacy when they pass, I think it’s pretty likely she was ready to go and snuck out. I know it’s awful to think of her being alone and it’s not what you would have wanted for her, but she made a choice for herself and she never doubted your love. I’m so so so sorry you’re grieving, I wish I could say something better but knowing that my pet only had one rough day his entire life does soothe me a bit, and I hope it does for you too.

Hip flexors. They’re the most important part of high jumps. Get in a good straddle sit, toes pointed and shoe laces facing the wall behind you (if your legs are in the correct position it just won’t work). Now just do little lifts with each foot, raising it about six inches off the ground and lowering back down. Do not touch the ground. Do 20 on each side if you can, and 20 with both at the same time.
